record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so I register new scientifically motivated comparisons while preserving existing unresolved robustness checks. The prior run established three very large dataset associations, but most other measured predictors remain either small or untested. I therefore add targeted biology and robustness questions.

First, I test MDM2 dependency through the p14ARF/MTAP/CDKN2A axis restricted to TP53-intact cells. CDKN2A encodes p14ARF, which inhibits MDM2; loss of CDKN2A could increase MDM2 pathway activity and therefore stronger MDM2 dependency, represented by a more negative dependency_MDM2 score. I register CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-intact and MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact in TP53-intact cells, both expected negative. MTAP is frequently co-deleted near CDKN2A and can proxy similar p14ARF/CDKN2A locus biology, so concordance would support a coherent axis; a large CDKN2A-only effect would favor CDKN2A-specific structure.

Second, I test more biologically selected RAS-pathway and RTK hypotheses. Direct KRAS-mutant versus wild-type effects were tiny, so I ask whether NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type cells predicts stronger KRAS dependency. NF1 loss activates RAS signaling, and in the absence of KRAS mutation this may reveal dependency on endogenous KRAS signaling. I also test ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type cells because KRAS mutation can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; an association in KRAS-wild-type cells would be more informative for RTK dependency than an unselected analysis.

Third, I refine MYC hypotheses. Amplification alone may be too blunt, so I restrict MYC-amplification effects to cells above a high MYC-expression threshold. DHX9, USP7, POLR2A, and RPL11 are plausible MYC-associated vulnerabilities involving replication stress, protein stability, transcription, and translation. If MYC amplification is a biologically meaningful driver state only when accompanied by high MYC expression, these expression-restricted effects may be larger than the near-null amplification-only effects. If they remain small, MYC amplification is unlikely to be a strong predictor of these dependencies in this dataset.

Fourth, I add specificity and robustness checks for the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. The prior STK11 co-loss interaction was near null, but a main effect restricted to STK11-intact cells can test whether the large positive effect is an artifact of KEAP1-STK11 co-deletion. I register KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact among STK11-intact cells, with the registered positive direction matching the accepted weaker-NFE2L2-dependency association.

Finally, I test screen-quality moderation using screen_roc_auc median split. For accepted SMARCA2 and WRN effects, a near-null interaction would support stability; a more negative interaction would suggest stronger associations in higher-quality screens. For the KEAP1/NFE2L2 positive association, I use positive interaction direction for the same logic. These are dataset-level robustness checks, not external-validity claims.

I prioritize comparisons with adequate expected cell counts and avoid structurally impossible strata. Large, precise main effects would motivate later validation; near-zero MYC or screen-quality interactions would mainly narrow the space of additional predictors and support robustness of the accepted associations. All claims remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable findings.

record.narrative: This wave mostly strengthens the robustness picture while producing one new biologically interesting MDM2 result and one unexpected opposite KRAS result. H99 is the strongest new finding: among TP53-intact cells, CDKN2A loss is associated with substantially stronger MDM2 dependency. The signed estimate is +0.1185 with CI [0.0793, 0.1577], meaning the raw CDKN2A-loss minus intact difference is approximately -0.119, i.e. more negative dependency. Relative to the MDM2 dependency mean magnitude (~0.269), even the lower bound is about a 29% difference, well above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. I accept H99 and request independent validation because it is a new, precise, mechanistically plausible association not yet externally checked in this run. H107 confirms that the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is not an artifact of STK11 co-loss: among STK11-intact cells, KEAP1 loss still shows a very large positive signed effect (+0.801, CI [0.779, 0.823]) for weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Given the already accepted and validated KEAP1/NFE2L2 main and TP53-stratified claims, I accept and close this as a context-specific robustness association. H100 remains unresolved because the MTAP-loss point effect is small (~+0.024 signed; raw stronger by 0.024, ~9% of MDM2 mean magnitude), but the upper CI bound allows a clinically meaningful effect. H101 rejects the registered prediction that NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type cells predicts stronger KRAS dependency; the interval is entirely negative for the signed hypothesis direction, implying raw exposed-minus-comparator is positive/less negative, i.e. weaker KRAS dependency. record.narrative: This synthesis reassesses the two response-deadline validations and the new independent validation for the CDKN2A/MDM2 association. All three are concordant and strengthen the supported dataset-specific finding set. H9 is explicitly reassessed using discovery R8 and validation R39. For the registered negative-direction claim that MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency, the independent validation is signed positive: estimate +0.8215, interval [0.7661, 0.8768]. Because estimates are already signed, this means the raw MSI-high-minus-non-MSI-high contrast is strongly negative, i.e. much more negative dependency_WRN and therefore much stronger WRN dependency. The magnitude is enormous relative to the WRN dependency mean of about -0.301; even the validation lower bound is far above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. Discovery R8 (+0.7899) and validation R39 are highly concordant, so H9 remains accepted and closed. H20 is reassessed using discovery R24 and validation R40. Among TP53-intact cells, KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact predicts weaker NFE2L2 dependency; validation is signed positive +0.7948, interval [0.7637, 0.8259], meaning the raw KEAP1-loss contrast is strongly positive and less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. This is essentially identical to discovery and far exceeds the 10% threshold. It also aligns with the independently validated TP53-loss stratum H26, making the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association large and robust across TP53 context. H99 is now accepted on independent validation. Among TP53-intact cells, CDKN2A loss versus intact predicts stronger MDM2 dependency; validation is signed positive +0.1162, interval [0.0584, 0.1741]. The raw interpretation is a negative MDM2 dependency difference of about 0.116, i.e. more negative dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. The validation lower bound is about 22% of the MDM2 dependency mean magnitude, comfortably above the 10% clinical-significance threshold, and discovery R54 (+0.1185) is concordant. I therefore accept H99 and close its investigation as a validated dataset-specific association. Overall supported findings: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The first three have independent validation and extensive context checks. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is robust across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, STK11-intact, library, and constructed-marker negative-control checks. The CDKN2A/MDM2 result is newly independently validated and mechanistically plausible through p14ARF/CDKN2A biology, although its dependence on MTAP co-deletion remains unresolved. Negative or null findings remain important: constructed marker D/E/F effects and many interactions are near null; ARID1A loss is not associated with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-intact cells; BRCA2 loss is not associated with WRN dependency among MSI-negative cells; ERBB2 amplification in KRAS-wild-type cells does not show a clinically meaningful effect; high-expression-restricted MYC-amplification effects on DHX9, POLR2A, and RPL11 are not supported; screen-quality, batch, culture, growth-rate, and several co-mutation interactions do not materially overturn the large main effects. The direct driver-marker effects tested so far, including KRAS mutation overall, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, and TP53 for MDM2, are generally small or not clinically meaningful in this dataset. Unresolved uncertainty remains for MTAP-independent effects, CDKN2A/MDM2 specificity in the absence of MTAP co-loss, whether CDKN2A effects persist when TP53 is lost, the post-hoc reversed NF1/KRAS observation, USP7 under high MYC expression, and many registered media, Cas9, ploidy, mutation-burden, and driver-context interactions. The most informative next analyses are the newly registered MDM2 specificity/TP53-context tests and the NF1/KRAS adenocarcinoma consistency test, followed by completing robustness interactions for the validated large effects and any already registered unresolved biological hypotheses. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable claims.

I also register TP53-loss, media-serum, and lineage-subtype context checks for the CDKN2A/MDM2 association. The TP53 interaction is particularly important because a near-null or positive interaction would support p14ARF specificity, whereas a large opposite-direction effect would indicate that the accepted TP53-intact association does not generalize across p53 context. The media and lineage checks are robustness/context tests, not external claims. Second, the unexpected post-hoc NF1/KRAS result showed weaker KRAS dependency with NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type cells. I register a more restrictive KRAS-wild-type/BRAF-wild-type test to see whether that opposite association survives removal of other MAPK drivers. Because KRAS, BRAF, and RAS-pathway dependencies can be bypassed by alternative RAS activation, this may be more interpretable than the broader KRAS-wild-type analysis. Third, NF1 loss could also shift dependency within the RAS network; I register NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type cells against RIT1 dependency, expecting stronger RIT1 dependency if endogenous RAS-pathway activation compensates for weaker KRAS dependency. Fourth, EGFR amplification effects were near threshold, so I test EGFR amplification among PIK3CA-wild-type cells. Fifth, direct driver-marker analyses for STAT3, DHX9, and USP7 remain sparse. The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

record.narrative: This wave produces two new very large dataset-specific associations and clarifies the CDKN2A/MDM2 result. H118 is the largest new finding: TP53 loss versus TP53 intact shows a strongly positive signed association with dependency_USP7 for the registered weaker-dependency direction, estimate +0.396 with 95% interval [0.325, 0.467]. Since estimates are already signed, the raw TP53-loss minus intact difference is positive, i.e. less negative dependency and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. Relative to the USP7 dependency mean magnitude (~0.175), the lower bound is roughly 1.9 times the mean, far above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. This is mechanistically plausible because USP7 is closely tied to p53/MDM2 biology, and p53 loss could reduce dependency on USP7. I accept H118 and request independent validation because it is a new, precise, mechanistically important claim. H116 is also a new large effect: PTEN loss versus PTEN intact shows a strong positive signed association for stronger STAT3 dependency, estimate +0.267, interval [0.215, 0.319]. Relative to the STAT3 dependency mean magnitude (~0.282), the lower bound is about 76% of the mean, so the evidence supports a clinically meaningful direction. I accept H116 and keep it active for context checks; PTEN/STAT3 is biologically plausible but less directly supported by prior negative STAT3 tests than the p53-USP7 finding. H112 shows that the CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency also appears among TP53-loss cells: signed estimate +0.111, interval [0.035, 0.186], with lower bound about 13% of the MDM2 mean. I accept H112 as a robust context-specific dataset association and close that stratum. H113 shows the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association among TP53-intact and MTAP-intact cells: signed estimate +0.106, interval [0.063, 0.149], lower bound about 23%. I accept H113 and close it as evidence that the accepted H99 result is not simply due to MTAP co-deletion. However, H124, the direct TP53-loss interaction, is near zero: signed estimate +0.008, interval [-0.077, 0.093]. The point estimate does not support a clinically meaningful interaction, but the interval is wide enough to allow important interaction in either direction, so I leave H124 unresolved and active. This means the CDKN2A/MDM2 association may not be p14ARF/TP53-specific in this dataset, contrary to a simple mechanistic expectation. H114 tests MTAP loss among TP53-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells; the signed effect is small, +0.009, interval [-0.015, 0.033]. The upper bound slightly exceeds a 10% threshold, but the point estimate is near null and the interval includes no effect, so I leave it unresolved rather than accepting or rejecting it. H119 tests whether the p14ARF/CDKN2A axis also predicts USP7 dependency among TP53-intact cells; the signed effect is essentially null, +0.003, interval [-0.019, 0.025]. The upper bound is near threshold and the point is negligible, so H119 is unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. The RIT1 test is negative for the proposed compensatory mechanism: H121 rejects the hypothesis that NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type cells strengthens RIT1 dependency; the signed estimate is -0.011 and the upper bound for the proposed direction is below the 10% threshold. The NF1/KRAS post-hoc observation remains suggestive but not acceptably precise: H123 is positive, +0.036, interval [0.003, 0.069], but the lower bound is far below the 10% threshold; H115 in adenocarcinoma includes null. Thus I keep H115 and H123 active/unresolved rather than accepting. EGFR amplification among PIK3CA-wild-type cells (H122) is in the expected direction but has a lower CI bound near null; BRCA2 loss for DHX9 (H120) is near null with an upper bound that still allows a meaningful effect. Both remain unresolved. Overall, the new accepted evidence strengthens a p53-related USP7 association and adds PTEN loss as a strong STAT3 dependency association, while showing CDKN2A/MDM2 is robust to MTAP-intact restriction and also present in the TP53-loss stratum. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or generalizable claims.

All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due, so this stage registers a new wave of targeted biological and specificity tests around the validated core associations and around outcomes that remain weakly characterized. The accepted large associations are SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency. The new proposals focus on the next most informative mechanisms and contexts. First, the CDKN2A/MDM2 result points to the p53-MDM2-USP7 axis. TP53 loss may weaken USP7 dependency because USP7 function is tied to the MDM2-p53 circuit, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells may also predict stronger USP7 dependency if p14ARF pathway effects extend across MDM2-regulating vulnerabilities. I also register TP53-loss, media-serum, and lineage-subtype context checks for the CDKN2A/MDM2 association. The TP53 interaction is particularly important because a near-null or positive interaction would support p14ARF specificity, whereas a large opposite-direction effect would indicate that the accepted TP53-intact association does not generalize across p53 context. The media and lineage checks are robustness/context tests, not external claims. Second, the unexpected post-hoc NF1/KRAS result showed weaker KRAS dependency with NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type cells. I register a more restrictive KRAS-wild-type/BRAF-wild-type test to see whether that opposite association survives removal of other MAPK drivers. Because KRAS, BRAF, and RAS-pathway dependencies can be bypassed by alternative RAS activation, this may be more interpretable than the broader KRAS-wild-type analysis. Third, NF1 loss could also shift dependency within the RAS network; I register NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type cells against RIT1 dependency, expecting stronger RIT1 dependency if endogenous RAS-pathway activation compensates for weaker KRAS dependency. Fourth, EGFR amplification effects were near threshold, so I test EGFR amplification among PIK3CA-wild-type cells. PIK3CA mutation may bypass EGFR dependence, making EGFR-amplified cells without PIK3CA mutation more likely to show clinically meaningful EGFR dependency. Fifth, direct driver-marker analyses for STAT3, DHX9, and USP7 remain sparse. PIK3CA mutation was near null for STAT3, so PTEN loss provides a complementary PI3K/AKT-pathway hypothesis, and SMAD4 loss provides a TGF-beta/noncanonical STAT3 hypothesis. BRCA2 loss is tested against DHX9 dependency because replication stress and helicase-related vulnerabilities are plausible but not yet supported in this dataset. These proposals are chosen to have binary exposures with adequate expected cell sizes and to test hypotheses where a 10-percent relative effect would be scientifically meaningful. All remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects or generalizable claims.","analyze":"No assessments are due, so I request twelve previously registered comparisons that are most informative now. First, the accepted CDKN2A/MDM2 association in TP53-intact cells needs specificity and context analysis. H112 tests whether the same CDKN2A-loss effect persists when TP53 is lost. If the effect disappears in TP53-loss cells, that supports a p14ARF/TP53-specific mechanism; if it persists, p53 may not be required or the association may reflect a broader genomic effect. H113 tests CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact and MTAP-intact cells to determine whether the CDKN2A association is specific rather than driven by nearby MTAP co-deletion. H114 tests MTAP loss among TP53-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells to assess whether MTAP has an independent effect on MDM2 dependency. H124 quantifies the TP53-context interaction directly, giving an estimate of whether CDKN2A affects MDM2 dependency differently in TP53-loss versus TP53-intact cells. Second, I extend the p53-MDM2 axis to USP7, another regulator of p53/MDM2 biology. H118 tests TP53-loss versus TP53-intact cells for weaker USP7 dependency, and H119 tests CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for stronger USP7 dependency, allowing me to determine whether the MDM2 result is part of a broader p14ARF/p53-USP7 circuit or is MDM2-specific. Third, the unexpected NF1-loss versus KRAS-dependency observation needs independent-style consistency checks within this dataset. H115 tests the reversed NF1-loss effect among adenocarcinoma KRAS-wild-type cells, while H123 tests it among KRAS-wild-type cells that are also BRAF-wild-type, removing a major MAPK driver bypass. H121 tests NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type cells for stronger RIT1 dependency, addressing whether reduced KRAS dependency is accompanied by compensatory dependency on another RAS-family node. Fourth, I test selected pathway-specific hypotheses that could reveal clinically meaningful effects masked in unselected analyses: EGFR amplification among PIK3CA-wild-type cells, where downstream bypass is less likely; BRCA2 loss for DHX9 dependency, a plausible replication-stress vulnerability; and PTEN loss for STAT3 dependency, a PI3K/AKT-STAT3 hypothesis after the PIK3CA result was near null. All selected analyses are existing claims and use the supplied dataset only. These are associations, not causal claims or external generalizability claims. If any effect is directionally coherent and its uncertainty is compatible with a clinically meaningful relative difference, I will consider it in appraise; if it is new, precise, and mechanistically important, I may then consider validation.","appraise":"This wave produces two new very large dataset-specific associations and clarifies the CDKN2A/MDM2 result. H118 is the largest new finding: TP53 loss versus TP53 intact shows a strongly positive signed association with dependency_USP7 for the registered weaker-dependency direction, estimate +0.396 with 95% interval [0.325, 0.467]. Since estimates are already signed, the raw TP53-loss minus intact difference is positive, i.e. less negative dependency and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. Relative to the USP7 dependency mean magnitude (~0.175), the lower bound is roughly 1.9 times the mean, far above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. This is mechanistically plausible because USP7 is closely tied to p53/MDM2 biology, and p53 loss could reduce dependency on USP7. I accept H118 and request independent validation because it is a new, precise, mechanistically important claim. H116 is also a new large effect: PTEN loss versus PTEN intact shows a strong positive signed association for stronger STAT3 dependency, estimate +0.267, interval [0.215, 0.319]. Relative to the STAT3 dependency mean magnitude (~0.282), the lower bound is about 76% of the mean, so the evidence supports a clinically meaningful direction. I accept H116 and keep it active for context checks; PTEN/STAT3 is biologically plausible but less directly supported by prior negative STAT3 tests than the p53-USP7 finding. H112 shows that the CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency also appears among TP53-loss cells: signed estimate +0.111, interval [0.035, 0.186], with lower bound about 13% of the MDM2 mean. I accept H112 as a robust context-specific dataset association and close that stratum. H113 shows the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association among TP53-intact and MTAP-intact cells: signed estimate +0.106, interval [0.063, 0.149], lower bound about 23%. I accept H113 and close it as evidence that the accepted H99 result is not simply due to MTAP co-deletion. However, H124, the direct TP53-loss interaction, is near zero: signed estimate +0.008, interval [-0.077, 0.093]. The point estimate does not support a clinically meaningful interaction, but the interval is wide enough to allow important interaction in either direction, so I leave H124 unresolved and active. This means the CDKN2A/MDM2 association may not be p14ARF/TP53-specific in this dataset, contrary to a simple mechanistic expectation. H114 tests MTAP loss among TP53-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells; the signed effect is small, +0.009, interval [-0.015, 0.033]. The upper bound slightly exceeds a 10% threshold, but the point estimate is near null and the interval includes no effect, so I leave it unresolved rather than accepting or rejecting it. H119 tests whether the p14ARF/CDKN2A axis also predicts USP7 dependency among TP53-intact cells; the signed effect is essentially null, +0.003, interval [-0.019, 0.025]. The upper bound is near threshold and the point is negligible, so H119 is unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. The RIT1 test is negative for the proposed compensatory mechanism: H121 rejects the hypothesis that NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type cells strengthens RIT1 dependency; the signed estimate is -0.011 and the upper bound for the proposed direction is below the 10% threshold. The NF1/KRAS post-hoc observation remains suggestive but not acceptably precise: H123 is positive, +0.036, interval [0.003, 0.069], but the lower bound is far below the 10% threshold; H115 in adenocarcinoma includes null. Thus I keep H115 and H123 active/unresolved rather than accepting. This corrected explore form registers refinements and new comparisons without leaving refinements in an invalid state: whenever a proposal is linked to an earlier parent, I attach available motivating result IDs. For proposals whose parent had no direct evidence, such as the KIF18A/RB1 follow-up, I intentionally omit the parent link and register the context test as a new comparison. All proposed exposure contrasts use variables with adequate expected cell sizes and clear exposed/comparator definitions. record.narrative:
This appraise wave mostly tests robustness and specificity of previously accepted associations, and the central accepted associations remain strong. For PTEN loss and stronger STAT3 dependency, the effect is robust in three contexts: TP53-intact cells (H128, signed +0.287 [0.227,0.347]), PIK3CA-wild-type cells (H132, signed +0.267 [0.210,0.323]), and adenocarcinoma cells (H136, signed +0.268 [0.206,0.330]). The lower bounds are all many times the 10% absolute-mean benchmark for dependency_STAT3 (~0.282), so these are strong dataset-specific associations rather than fragile context artifacts. For TP53 loss and weaker USP7 dependency, the effect is robust in the dominant Avana library (H127, signed +0.405 [0.330,0.479]) and in MTAP-intact cells (H130, signed +0.421 [0.343,0.498]), far above the 10% benchmark for dependency_USP7 (~0.175). For CDKN2A loss and stronger MDM2 dependency, the association remains strong in PTEN-intact cells (H139, signed +0.116 [0.078,0.153]), again above the 10% benchmark for dependency_MDM2 (~0.269). These context acceptances should be interpreted as robustness checks within the supplied dataset, not as mechanistic causality claims.

The direct interaction tests are less decisive. The USP7 TP53-loss effect does not show evidence of moderation by CDKN2A loss (H131, signed -0.004 [-0.177,0.170]); the interval is wide and allows clinically meaningful interaction in either direction, so this remains unresolved rather than rejected. The CDKN2A/MDM2 lineage interaction is also near null and imprecise (H126, signed -0.010 [-0.088,0.068]); the accepted CDKN2A/MDM2 association does not require lineage-specific moderation, so I defer further follow-up. SMAD4 loss and STAT3 dependency is near null with wide uncertainty (H117, signed +0.011 [-0.026,0.047]); the upper bound allows a meaningful effect, but the evidence is not supportive, so it is deferred.

H135 is rejected as originally registered: TP53 loss was not associated with stronger DHX9 dependency. The signed interval is entirely negative, meaning the raw contrast is positive (TP53 loss associated with weaker DHX9 dependency), but the raw magnitude interval is small (~0.001 to 0.039) and only the upper portion crosses the 10% benchmark for dependency_DHX9. I therefore do not accept the opposite direction, but I register it as a new exploratory reversal linked to H135 because the raw interval is on one side of zero. H146 and H147 are inconclusive: RB1 loss among faster-growing cells and BRCA2 loss for POLR2A have intervals that include both null and potentially meaningful effects, but point estimates are small; I defer them. Overall, the most important pending action is independent validation of the main PTEN/STAT3 association (H116), which remains unvalidated despite strong context support.

This corrected explore form registers refinements and new comparisons without leaving refinements in an invalid state: whenever a proposal is linked to an earlier parent, I attach available motivating result IDs. For proposals whose parent had no direct evidence, such as the KIF18A/RB1 follow-up, I intentionally omit the parent link and register the context test as a new comparison. The scientific plan has two purposes. First, it checks whether the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations remain robust in biologically meaningful contexts: PTEN loss and STAT3 in adenocarcinoma and high IFN-gamma; TP53 loss and USP7 in high MYC-expression cells; CDKN2A loss and MDM2 in PTEN-intact cells; MSI-high and WRN in high IFN-gamma; SMARCA4 loss and SMARCA2 in high AXL; KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 in high hypoxia. record.narrative:
Final synthesis at this checkpoint focuses on the two due validation results and then places them within the broader evidence set.

H99 is accepted and closed. The hypothesis is that CDKN2A loss is associated with more negative MDM2 dependency score, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency, among TP53-intact cells. Because the claim direction is -1, the positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative. Discovery R54 estimated +0.1185 [0.0793, 0.1577]; independent validation R66 estimated +0.1162 [0.0584, 0.1741]. These are highly concordant in magnitude and precision. Relative to the average absolute MDM2 dependency score, the validation lower bound is far above the 10% practical benchmark, and the point estimate is very large in dependency-score units. This is one of the most robust dataset-specific associations discovered: CDKN2A-loss cells show stronger MDM2 dependency, with consistency across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, MTAP-intact, and PTEN-intact contexts.

H116 is accepted and closed. The hypothesis is that PTEN loss is associated with more negative STAT3 dependency score, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency. With direction -1, the positive signed estimates indicate the raw contrast is in the hypothesized direction. Discovery R78 estimated +0.2674 [0.2153, 0.3195]; independent validation R93 estimated +0.2770 [0.1967, 0.3572]. The validation lower bound remains far above 10% of the average absolute STAT3 dependency score, and the effect is stable in TP53-intact, PIK3CA-wild-type, and adenocarcinoma contexts. I therefore treat PTEN loss as a strongly supported predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency within this supplied dataset, without implying causality or external generalizability.

Supported dataset-specific findings now center on five biologically coherent axes: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, robust across TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata and several context subsets; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, independently validated and robust across p53/MTAP/PTEN contexts; TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, independently validated and robust in the dominant library and MTAP-intact strata; and PTEN loss with much stronger STAT3 dependency, now independently validated and robust across TP53-intact, PIK3CA-wild-type, and adenocarcinoma contexts.

Negative or unsupported findings include: no support for the original hypothesis that NF1 loss strengthens KRAS dependency among KRAS-wild-type cells, and no support that NF1 loss strengthens RIT1 dependency in the same setting; no support that MYC amplification is a simple predictor of stronger POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, or USP7 dependency; no meaningful association of the arbitrary research markers D/E/F with SMARCA2, WRN, or NFE2L2 dependency; and little evidence that technical screen-quality or batch-like variables strongly moderate the largest accepted biological associations, although some interaction intervals remain wide.

Unresolved uncertainty remains. The opposite-direction NF1-loss effects on KRAS dependency among KRAS-wild-type cells (H111/H123) have positive intervals but lower bounds below the practical 10% benchmark and are post-hoc relative to the original hypotheses, so they are deferred rather than accepted. The opposite-direction TP53-loss association with DHX9 dependency (H148) is similarly small and clinically uncertain. EGFR amplification in PIK3CA-wild-type cells (H122) shows an opposite-direction near-threshold signal, and the CDKN2A-loss/TP53-loss interaction for MDM2 (H124) and USP7 TP53-loss/CDKN2A-loss interaction (H131) are too imprecise to conclude effect modification. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only.

The most informative next analyses should refine and localize the accepted findings rather than repeatedly retest their overall existence. For SMARCA2, test whether ARID1A co-loss enhances the SMARCA4-loss effect. For USP7, stratify the TP53-loss effect by CDKN2A-loss status. For STAT3, test PTEN-loss effects and interactions within PIK3CA-mutant biology and TP53-loss strata. For NFE2L2, extend the KEAP1-loss association into MTAP-loss strata. For pathway-driver dependencies, test EGFR and ERBB2 dependency among KRAS/BRAF-wild-type cells and KRAS dependency among BRAF/EGFR-wild-type cells to determine whether apparent null effects are masked by co-occurring driver pathways. Independent validation remains valuable only for newly accepted strong effects or sharply refined context hypotheses; low-priority small opposite-direction effects should not consume validation budget.

prompt:
Iteration 8/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: Due validation assessment. H118 is accepted and closed: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. The original discovery contrast R71 was +0.396 [0.325, 0.467], and independent validation R79 is +0.380 [0.269, 0.491]. Because the hypothesis direction is +1, these signed estimates mean the raw TP53-loss exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive, i.e. TP53-loss cell lines have less negative USP7 dependency scores. The magnitude is many-fold larger than a practical 10%-of-average-absolute-score benchmark for dependency_USP7, and discovery and validation are highly concordant despite multiplicity-adjusted validation intervals. This is now a robustly supported dataset-specific association. H133 is accepted and closed: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency among TP53-loss cell lines. Discovery R99 was +0.190 [0.085, 0.296] and independent validation R106 is +0.243 [0.087, 0.400]. With direction -1, the raw contrast is negative, so PTEN-null lines have more negative STAT3 dependency scores. Although this TP53-loss stratum is smaller and somewhat less precise than the overall PTEN effect, the lower bound remains clearly above the practical clinical-significance benchmark, so I accept it as a dataset-specific subgroup-supported finding without claiming causality. H109 remains rejected and closed: there is no support for a clinically meaningful interaction in which MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency specifically in high screen_roc_auc strata. Discovery R64 was essentially null and opposite to the hypothesized direction, and validation R80 is also small and opposite (-0.012 [-0.105, 0.082]), crossing zero. The interval is wide enough that exact absence cannot be proven, but there is no positive evidence, so further resources are not warranted. H131 is left unresolved but closed: whether the TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency is modified by CDKN2A-loss status is not established. Discovery R86 was tiny, and validation R107 is -0.065 [-0.312, 0.182], very wide and opposite to the tested interaction direction. This neither confirms nor excludes effect modification with sufficient precision, but the tested hypothesis is not supported and should not consume further validation or focused analysis unless a new mechanistic rationale emerges. Overall, the supplied dataset now supports a coherent set of measured associations: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Several of these are robust across TP53/MTAP/CDKN2A/PIK3CA/adenocarcinoma/library/culture contexts already tested. Negative or unsupported findings include the original hypotheses that ERBB2 amplification predicts stronger ERBB2 dependency, NF1 loss predicts stronger KRAS or RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wild-type cells, MYC amplification is a simple predictor of POLR2A/RPL11/DHX9/USP7 dependency, or arbitrary research markers D/E/F predict SMARCA2, WRN, or NFE2L2 dependency. EGFR amplification as a predictor of TMED10 dependency and RB1 loss as a predictor of KIF18A dependency remain near null or underpowered. Unresolved uncertainty remains around some near-threshold opposite-direction or driver-stratified contrasts, including EGFR amplification in PIK3CA-wild-type cells, weak opposite-direction NF1-loss effects on KRAS dependency, small TP53-loss associations with DHX9, and several moderator interactions with wide intervals. The next most informative analyses are therefore localization and robustness rather than repeated overall testing: culture-type and serum strata for the accepted axes, and driver-null stratified tests of EGFR, ERBB2, TMED10, and KIF18A dependencies. Remaining validation capacity should be reserved for newly accepted high-magnitude associations, not for near-null post-hoc effects. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal effects or claims of external generalizability.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Iteration 9/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
The new results strongly extend several accepted dependency axes into biologically interesting contexts. H141 shows that within AXL-high cells, SMARCA4 loss remains associated with a much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.789 with 95% interval [0.762, 0.815], direction -1, so the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is strongly negative. This is far above any practical 10% benchmark and has adequate cell sizes, so I accept and close it as a context-specific localization of the SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association. H142 shows the same robustness for KEAP1 loss in hypoxia-high cells: signed +0.784 [0.755, 0.814] in the direction indicating weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H165 shows MSI-high cells with high aneuploidy retain the very large stronger WRN dependency: signed +0.801 [0.761, 0.841], although the exposed cell count is smaller (65), so independent validation is useful. H184 shows PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in EMT-high cells: signed +0.262 [0.186, 0.338], again many times the clinical-significance benchmark. These four are accepted as supplied-dataset associations, not causal claims.

The exploratory receptor and pathway-specificity tests were mostly near null or inconclusive. H164, EGFR amplification as a predictor of weaker ERBB2 dependency, gives signed +0.0116 [-0.0137, 0.0369]. The point estimate is tiny and crosses zero; the upper bound permits a small effect near/above threshold, but the evidence is too weak and inconsistent with prior ERBB2-null findings to accept. I leave it unresolved and deferred. H178 and H186 test CDKN2A-loss specificity beyond MDM2: CDKN2A loss is not associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, signed -0.013 [-0.033, 0.007], and not with stronger KRAS dependency, signed -0.011 [-0.031, 0.009]. Both point in the opposite direction from the hypothesized stronger-dependency claims, and the intervals exclude clinically meaningful support in the stated direction; therefore I reject those stated hypotheses without excluding small opposite effects. H179 RB1 loss in high-ploidy KIF18A cells is near null with an imprecise interval; H180 CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact RPL11 cells, H181 BRCA2 loss in MSI-normal POLR2A cells, H185 MYC amplification for TMED10, and H187 BRAF V600E for weaker RIT1 dependency are all small-point, zero-crossing contrasts. Their upper bounds can admit modest positive effects, but the observed evidence does not justify accepting them. I keep them unresolved and deferred rather than spending resources on low-priority near-null effects. I request validation only for H165 because it is a newly accepted context-specific claim with the smallest exposed cell count among the accepted new results.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
