record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency contrast is more negative, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw contrast is less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. H192/R121 shows MSI-high lines retain an extremely large stronger WRN dependency even among low-aneuploidy lines: signed +0.776 [0.733, 0.820]. The lower bound is far above any plausible 10% benchmark for WRN dependency, so I accept and close it as a supplied-dataset context-specific localization. H197 is a duplicate of canonical H192 on the same evidence, so I do not assess H197 separately to avoid a canonical double assessment. H195/R122 localizes the PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency to hypoxia-high lines: signed +0.239 [0.166, 0.312], accept. H196/R123 localizes the SMARCA4-loss-associated much stronger SMARCA2 dependency to stemness-high lines: signed +0.781 [0.752, 0.810], accept. H198/R124 localizes the KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency to low-hypoxia lines: signed +0.809 [0.781, 0.837], accept. H199/R125 localizes the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency to EMT-high lines: signed +0.356 [0.255, 0.458], accept. These are very large dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

The mechanistic MTAP-loss interaction test H201/R126 is suggestive but imprecise: the signed interaction is +0.056 [-0.046, 0.158]. The point estimate favors stronger CDKN2A-loss-associated MDM2 dependency in MTAP-loss cells relative to MTAP-intact cells among TP53-intact lines, and the upper bound is potentially clinically meaningful, but the interval includes zero and the exposed interaction cell is small (68). I keep it unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. I request independent validation instead for H205/R130, because H205 is the most promising borderline new predictor claim: BRCA2 loss and stronger POLR2A dependency in TP53-intact lines has signed estimate +0.030 [-0.006, 0.066]. The point estimate is near or above a rough 10% relative threshold for POLR2A dependency, the interval crosses zero only slightly, and validation could decide whether this is a real supplied-dataset association rather than continue near-null exploration.

H202/R127 tests EGFR amplification in KRAS-wildtype adenocarcinoma and gives signed +0.019 [-0.018, 0.055]. The point estimate is small and zero-crossing, although the upper bound leaves a modest possible effect; I leave it unresolved and deferred. H203/R128 gives a small opposite-signed point for STK11 loss as a predictor of stronger KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype lines: signed -0.008 [-0.031, 0.015]. The upper bound is below a rough 10% threshold for KRAS dependency, so I reject and close the stated stronger-dependency hypothesis. H204/R129 is imprecise and opposite-signed for RB1 loss in TP53-loss lines: signed -0.020 [-0.074, 0.033]. The upper bound barely permits a clinically meaningful effect, so I leave it unresolved and deferred. H206/R131 shows no support for TP53 loss as a predictor of weaker RPL11 dependency: signed +0.004 [-0.016, 0.024]; the interval upper bound is approximately at or below a 10% threshold, so reject and close. H207/R132 gives no support for ERBB2 amplification predicting stronger ERBB2 dependency in EGFR-amplification-negative adenocarcinoma: signed -0.013 [-0.047, 0.021], with an opposite point and upper bound below the approximate threshold; reject and close.

Discovery R110 and independent validation R120 show a very large MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency in high-aneuploidy cells: signed +0.801 [0.761,0.841] and +0.778 [0.708,0.848], respectively. The exposed cell counts are smaller in this stratum, but both intervals are far from zero and the independent lower bound remains >0.70, confirming that the earlier accepted context-specific effect was not a small-sample artifact. Overall, the dataset now supports several high-magnitude measured associations: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, especially where p53/MTAP contexts are tested; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Many accepted effects persist across driver-status, lineage, library, culture/medium, and expression/stress strata already examined. record.narrative: Validation deadlines were assessed. H133, PTEN loss versus TP53-intact/loss and STAT3 dependency within TP53-loss lines, is accepted and closed. Discovery R99 and independent validation R106 are both strongly positive in the registered stronger-dependency direction: signed +0.190 [0.085, 0.296] and +0.243 [0.087, 0.400], respectively. Even the multiplicity-adjusted validation lower bound is far above a practical 10%-style threshold for these dependency scores, so the supplied dataset robustly supports PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss contexts, as an association rather than a causal claim. H131, the TP53-loss interaction with CDKN2A loss for weaker USP7 dependency, is not supported by validation and remains unresolved/deferred. Discovery R86 was essentially null in the claimed direction, signed -0.004 [-0.177, 0.170], and validation R107 is negative and very imprecise, signed -0.065 [-0.312, 0.182]. The data therefore do not support a positive CDKN2A-loss-dependent interaction of TP53 loss on USP7 dependency, but the validation interval is too wide to resolve whether a small or opposite interaction exists; this is deprioritized. H205, BRCA2 loss and stronger POLR2A dependency in TP53-intact lines, also remains unresolved/deferred. Discovery R130 was borderline, signed +0.030 [-0.006, 0.066], but independent validation R133 is near null, signed +0.004 [-0.061, 0.069]. For practical interpretation, this is an unsupported or at best very weak association; it should not be treated as an accepted finding. The adjusted interval leaves a small-to-moderate effect technically possible, so the formal status remains unresolved rather than a precise null, but it is no longer a priority axis. Overall, the strongest dataset-supported associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. These have replicated or held across many molecular, lineage, medium, library, stress-context, and quality stratifications already tested. Negative or unsupported findings include broad driver hypotheses such as ERBB2 amplification predicting stronger ERBB2 dependency, NF1 loss predicting stronger KRAS or RIT1 dependency, MYC amplification predicting POLR2A/RPL11/DHX9/TMED10 dependency, CDKN2A loss predicting stronger KRAS/KIF18A dependency, and the null research-marker panels. Future work should avoid additional broad near-null scanning and instead focus on resolving accepted axes or the few borderline mechanistic interactions: MTAP context for USP7/TP53, TP53-loss/adenocarcinoma localization for PTEN-STAT3, and whether TP53 status modifies BRCA2-POLR2A effects. No new validation requests remain, so future work should be discovery-based and tightly targeted.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I register twelve targeted mean_difference tests that localize already accepted dataset-specific dependency axes into biologically distinct contexts rather than broad near-null scanning. Direction conventions follow earlier claims: direction -1 represents stronger dependency and direction +1 represents weaker dependency, because dependency scores are more negative when stronger; anticipated_direction is the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before evidence. For SMARCA2, SMARCA4 loss is tested within low- and high-aneuploidy strata to determine whether the very strong accepted effect spans aneuploidy status. For WRN, MSI-high status is tested in high- and low-hypoxia strata. For NFE2L2, KEAP1 loss is tested in STK11-loss cells and in high mutation-burden cells to examine pathway co-alteration and mutation-burden context. For USP7, TP53 loss is tested in high- and low-mutation-burden strata. For STAT3, PTEN loss is tested in high mutation burden and in low hypoxia as a complement to the accepted high-hypoxia result. For MDM2, CDKN2A loss is tested among TP53-intact cells with STK11 or KEAP1 co-alteration to refine the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis into co-altered molecular contexts. These are associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability. In later appraisal, results should be accepted only when the signed 95% interval excludes zero and the lower bound is large relative to the approximate 10% practical benchmark; near-null or zero-crossing results should be deferred or closed rather than repeatedly explored.

Iteration 11/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency. H213 and H214 show that SMARCA4 loss is associated with very strong SMARCA2 dependency in both low- and high-aneuploidy strata: signed +0.791 [0.764,0.817] and +0.775 [0.747,0.803]. The lower bounds are far above zero and above a practical 10%-relative benchmark for dependency scores of this scale, so both are accepted and closed as supplied-dataset context localizations. Similarly, H215 and H216 show that MSI-high lines retain very strong WRN dependency across hypoxia-low and hypoxia-high contexts: signed +0.781 [0.740,0.822] and +0.798 [0.755,0.841]. Both are accepted and closed. H217 and H218 show KEAP1 loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency in STK11-loss and high-mutation-burden contexts: signed +0.775 [0.727,0.823] and +0.798 [0.770,0.826]. Both lower bounds are extremely strong, so both are accepted and closed. H219 and H220 show TP53 loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency in both high- and low-mutation-burden strata: signed +0.477 [0.379,0.575] and +0.315 [0.213,0.417]. Even the lower bounds are large relative to the outcome scale, so both are accepted and closed. H221 and H222 show PTEN loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in high mutation burden and low hypoxia contexts: signed +0.301 [0.227,0.375] and +0.290 [0.216,0.365]. These are clinically substantial by the supplied-dataset 10%-relative benchmark and are accepted and closed. H223 is suggestive but weaker: CDKN2A loss associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact STK11-loss lines gave signed +0.099 [0.017,0.180], with only 54 exposed lines. The interval excludes zero, but the lower bound is below a conservative 10%-relative benchmark for MDM2 dependency and the estimate is sensitive to a small cell, so it is kept unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H224 tests CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact KEAP1-loss lines and is not supported: signed +0.077 [-0.009,0.162], interval crosses zero and exposed cell is small. The upper bound leaves a clinically relevant effect possible, so I avoid a precise null and keep it unresolved/deferred. These accepted findings are associations within this supplied dataset only, not causal claims or externally generalizable claims; co-alteration structure and unmodeled technical factors could influence contexts, but the accepted effects are very large and pre-planned as localizations of already supported axes. No validation request is made because no new validation budget remains.

record.narrative:
I assessed the due validation response for H165. In the supplied dataset, MSI-high lines showed a very large and clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association for WRN within the high-aneuploidy stratum: the independent validation estimate is signed +0.778 in the registered stronger-dependency direction, with an adjusted 95% interval [0.708, 0.848]. This is consistent with the discovery estimate signed +0.801 [0.761, 0.841]. Even the lower bound is far above a conservative practical benchmark for these dependency scores, so H165 remains accepted and closed. The MSI-high/WRN axis therefore persists not only overall and in adenocarcinoma/adherent/Avana contexts, but also across low- and high-aneuploidy and low- and high-hypoxia strata tested so far. This is a dataset-specific association, not a causal claim or an external generalization.

I also reassessed H205 as part of final synthesis. BRCA2 loss was associated only weakly with stronger POLR2A dependency in TP53-intact lines at discovery (signed +0.030 [-0.006, 0.066]), and independent validation was near null (signed +0.004 [-0.061, 0.069]). The combined evidence does not support a scientifically meaningful BRCA2-loss-associated POLR2A dependency effect in TP53-intact lines, so I reject and close H205 rather than continue treating it as a priority unresolved axis.

The strongest supported supplied-dataset dependency axes are: (1) SMARCA4 loss is associated with very strong SMARCA2 dependency, replicated with validation and stable across adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-intact, library, medium, stress-score, and aneuploidy contexts; (2) MSI-high is associated with very strong WRN dependency, replicated with validation and stable across lineage, culture, library, hypoxia, and aneuploidy contexts; (3) KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, replicated with validation and stable across TP53, STK11, MTAP, library, hypoxia, mutation-burden, and other molecular contexts; (4) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, replicated with validation and robust in TP53-intact and TP53-loss settings, though co-altered STK11-loss and KEAP1-loss refinements remain uncertain; (5) TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, replicated with validation and present in both high- and low-mutation-burden strata, MTAP-intact and CDKN2A contexts; and (6) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, replicated with validation and preserved across TP53 states, adenocarcinoma, PIK3CA, EMT, hypoxia, and mutation-burden contexts.

The main negative or unsupported findings are also clear. Matched driver-gene dependency hypotheses were largely not supported: KRAS mutation did not establish stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E was not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification did not robustly support stronger EGFR dependency; and ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger ERBB2 dependency in overall or refined contexts. MYC amplification and MYC-expression contexts did not support DHX9, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, or USP7 dependency. RB1 loss was not supported as a strong KIF18A dependency predictor, CDKN2A loss was not associated with stronger KRAS or KIF18A dependency overall, and the constructed research markers D/E/F behaved as null panels. BRCA2 loss was not a meaningful WRN predictor among MSI-negative lines and is now rejected for TP53-intact POLR2A dependency.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly in interaction/context modification of the major axes, not in the main effects themselves. The TP53-loss-by-CDKN2A-loss interaction for USP7 remains unresolved because validation was wide and imprecise. MTAP-loss context for TP53-loss USP7, MTAP-related MDM2/CDKN2A interactions, PTEN-by-TP53 or adenocarcinoma localization of STAT3 dependency, and several borderline MDM2 co-alteration contexts remain unresolved. The most informative next analyses are not broad scans but these existing targeted follow-ups: CDKN2A loss effect on MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact MTAP-loss lines (H129), TP53-loss USP7 dependency in MTAP-loss lines and MTAP-loss interaction hypotheses (H182/H210), PTEN-loss STAT3 interactions and TP53/adenocarcinoma localizations (H154/H159/H208/H209), and limited MDM2 co-loss context refinement (H223/H224). No validation budget remains, so further work should be discovery-based and tightly targeted to these axes.
